raw_response:
My wheat is already in the ground from last October — I sowed about 8 mu of improved winter wheat, same as always. Right now it's greening up after winter, so I'm getting ready for the spring topdressing. The extension fellow told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu at jointing, but I usually put a bit more, around 18 kg, because last year I held back and the yield dropped. I'll spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer as base plus another 40 jin of urea at topdressing. That gives me roughly 32 kg of nitrogen, 22 kg of phosphorus, and 7 kg of potassium per mu all together. I irrigate three times for wheat — once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Water costs money now with the meters, so I don't do more than that unless it's very dry. For pests, I spray herbicide once in spring and fungicide once if I see rust, plus insecticide twice — about four sprays total. I rotary-tilled before planting last fall, so that's done.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I'll plant summer maize right away on the same 8 mu. No time for ploughing — I'll use no-tillage direct seeding, same as everyone else in the village. I buy hybrid maize seed, one bag per mu, costs about 60 yuan. For maize I put down less fertilizer than wheat, around 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, which is about 22 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium. I irrigate twice for maize if the rain doesn't come, and spray insecticide twice plus herbicide once. If things go normal, I expect about 1000 kg per mu for wheat and 1100 kg per mu for maize. I don't grow cotton anymore — too much labor, and at my age I'd rather stick with the wheat-maize rotation that I know.
